query: Chart the comparative specifications of the eight planets in our solar system in a structured table.
narrative:
The following table presents a comparative overview of the eight planets in our solar system, detailing key physical and orbital characteristics.

| Planet   | Mean Radius (km) | Mass (×10²⁴ kg) | Gravity (m/s²) | Orbital Period (Earth days) | Rotational Period (hours) | Distance from Sun (AU) | Number of Moons | Atmosphere Composition           |
|----------|------------------|------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| Mercury  | 2,439.7          | 0.330            | 3.7            | 87.97                       | 1,408                     | 0.39                  | 0               | Thin exosphere: helium, sodium   |
| Venus    | 6,051.8          | 4.87             | 8.87           | 224.70                      | -5,832                    | 0.72                  | 0               | Dense: carbon dioxide, nitrogen  |
| Earth    | 6,371.0          | 5.97             | 9.8            | 365.26                      | 24                        | 1.00                  | 1               | Nitrogen, oxygen                 |
| Mars     | 3,389.5          | 0.642            | 3.71           | 686.98                      | 24.6                      | 1.52                  | 2               | Thin: carbon dioxide, nitrogen   |
| Jupiter  | 69,911           | 1,898            | 23.1           | 4,332.59                    | 9.9                       | 5.20                  | 95              | Hydrogen, helium                 |
| Saturn   | 58,232           | 568              | 9.0            | 10,759.22                   | 10.7                      | 9.58                  | 146             | Hydrogen, helium                 |
| Uranus   | 25,362           | 86.8             | 8.7            | 30,688.5                    | -17.2                     | 19.18                 | 27              | Hydrogen, helium, methane        |
| Neptune  | 24,622           | 102              | 11.0           | 60,182                      | 16.1                      | 30.07                 | 16              | Hydrogen, helium, methane        |

**Notes:**

- **Rotational Period:** A negative value indicates retrograde rotation, meaning the planet rotates in the opposite direction to its orbit around the Sun.

- **Distance from Sun (AU):** One Astronomical Unit (AU) is the average distance from Earth to the Sun, approximately 149.6 million kilometers.

- **Atmosphere Composition:** The primary components of each planet's atmosphere are listed.

**Sources:**

- Mean radius, mass, gravity, orbital period, rotational period, and number of moons: ([planet-five.vercel.app](https://planet-five.vercel.app/?utm_source=openai))

- Distance from Sun and atmosphere composition: ([encyclopedia.com](https://www.encyclopedia.com/reference/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/major-planets-solar-system-table?utm_source=openai))

This table provides a concise comparison of the planets, highlighting their diverse characteristics and emphasizing the vast differences among them.
